**Step 1 — Scene:** A cheeseburger with a few fries and what appears to be a broiled lobster tail.

**Step 2 — Vessel:** A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** across. Area = 3.14 × 13² = **531 cm²**.

**Step 3 — Items:** Burger bun, beef patty, cheese, pickle slices and a little creamy sauce; several fries; lobster meat with a browned topping, still in its shell. The burger is calculated as one assembled item to avoid counting overlapping layers twice.

**Steps 4–7 — Area, volume, weight and energy:**

| Item | Plate area covered | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Assembled cheeseburger | 22% | 117 cm² | 4 cm | 468 ml | 0.50 g/ml | 234 g | 280 | 655 kcal |
| Lobster meat with browned topping | 10% | 53 cm² | 1.7 cm | 90 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 86 g | 160 | 138 kcal |
| French fries | 3% | 16 cm² | 1.2 cm | 19 ml | 0.65 g/ml | 12 g | 310 | 37 kcal |

The edible items cover approximately **35% of the plate**, with the lobster shell occupying a little additional area. The burger’s composite density accounts for its airy bun and denser fillings; no further volume reduction is applied. Lobster shell is excluded from edible weight.

**Step 8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **332 g and 830 kcal** is plausible for this burger, a modest amount of lobster meat, and only a few fries. The largest uncertainties are the burger’s thickness and the lobster topping.
